 3. Additional Collector, Seraikella-Kharsawan
 4. District Land Acquisition Officer, Seraikella-Kharsawan

 Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sujit Narayan Prasad
 ---------
For the Petitioners : Mr. Ashim Kr. Sahani, Adv.

For the Respondents : Ms. Piyushita Meha Tudu,
Ac to Aag-Iv
For the Nhai : Mrs. Sweety Topno, Advocate

Mr. Ashim Kr. Sahani, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that due to inadvertence, the National Highway Authority of India, has not been impleaded as party-respondent and as such, he has sought for leave of this Court to implead National Highway Authority of India as respondent no.5 in course of the day.
Mrs. Sweety Topno, appears for the National Highway Authority of India, waives notice on their behalf.
This writ petition is under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, whereby and whereunder, the direction has been sought for to refer the matter before the Arbitrator so as to decide the grievance of the writ petitioners regarding the quantum of compensation in the light of the provision as contained under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

entities.text: Madhusudan Das vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mrs. Sweety Topno, learned counsel appearing for the National Highway Authority of India has submitted that this writ petition may be disposed of by directing the respondent no.4 for referring the objection raised by the writ petitioners with respect to amount of compensation before the Arbitrator.

This Court after having heard the learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the provision as contained under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 and since the writ petitioners have also made objection showing their dissatisfaction with respect to quantum of compensation, is hereby disposing of the writ petition by directing the respondent no.4 to refer the said objection before the Arbitrator, so the dispute will be decided in view of the provision as contained under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
Accordingly, let such decision be taken within the period of eight weeks' from the date of receipt of copy of the order.
In view thereof, this writ petition stands disposed of.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) Rohit/-
